podcast.body: This rather slow song from the album "Blood and Chocolate" became its best-remembered track, despite the album's overall bruising and raucous nature. It is a sinister piece exploring romantic obsession, often mistaken for a traditional love song, with Attractions bassist Bruce Thomas describing it as "neurotic." The song remains one of Costello's most covered compositions, notably performed by Fiona Apple live with Costello on stage at a VH1 event. "The sinister I Want You. Appeared to romantic obsession that many mistook for a love song."

podcast.body: This song, from the album "Blood and Chocolate," holds the distinction of being the longest track in Elvis Costello's extensive catalog. The album itself was a reunion with The Attractions and was lauded by fans for its return to a more traditional Costello sound. "This album also contained the longest song in the Elvis catalog. It's called I Want You."
